items.title: Local embeddability versus embeddability under choice, and local isomorphism versus elementary equivalence
items.author: Supakun Panasawatwong; J. K. Truss
items.difficulty_reason: The lemma collects three comparisons for omega-trees with finite levels: under the axiom of choice local embeddability coincides with embeddability, under the axiom of choice local isomorphism coincides with isomorphism, and unconditionally local isomorphism coincides with elementary equivalence (statement lines 631-637). The first two clauses turn a local embedding into a genuine one by building the tree of finite approximations and applying Konig's lemma, which is where the axiom of choice enters (proof lines 640-646). The third clause is a two-way comparison of finite initial segments: elementary equivalence is transported into an isomorphism of each pair of finite initial segments by a sentence that pins down the first n levels, and the converse is a back-and-forth argument in which the answer strategy is built from the given local isomorphisms (proof lines 648-659). The content is in the third clause, since it is the only one that does not simply unwrap the definitions with a compactness argument. H2.
